newsitem.title: NICARAGUA: Nicaragua to change crazy street addresses.
newsitem.headline: Nicaragua to change crazy street addresses.

text.p: Postal authorites on Friday said they were going to modernise Nicaragua's unique system of identifying street addresses, long a nightmare to tourists and letter carriers.
In Nicaragua the streets have no names, and few houses have numbers. Houses are identified by landmarks and city blocks.
A typical address is: "From where the old Pepsi plant was, one block toward the lake, two blocks down."
"Down" and "up" are really west and east to local residents.

Sometimes addresses even include landmarks that no longer exist. For example, one point of referrence is "from coconut trees." Even though the trees were cut down, Managuans continue using them in their addresses.
Stressed pizza delivery boys and letter carriers sometimes drive up and down streets knocking on doors to find addresses.

The general manager of the postal monopoly Correos de Nicaragua, Jose Ernesto Gonzalez, told Reuters under the new system each house will have a seven-digit postal code to identify its region, district, zone and block. The house's number or identification will precede the code.
